name: Molet
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page mole1239 'Molet' and reference record 311276 (hh:w:Carteretal:Mur, hhtype wordlist)
sources.note: Bibliography contains a single item (Carter et al. 2012); comment: discovered on survey, close to Asaro'o [mtv] but not intelligible with it.
404 - no Molet entry (Asaro'o entry holds only McElhanon & Voorhoeve 1970 wordlist items).

sources.citation: Carter, John, Katie Carter, John Grummitt, Bonnie MacKenzie & Janell Masters. 2012. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Mur Village Vernaculars. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2012-043. Dallas: SIL International. 71 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Appendix B.2 'Characteristics of Mur Molet' (pp.42-43) gives only a phone chart (Fig. 4 'Mur Molet phones'), possessive and verb suffix tables, SOV word order; no mention of stress, accent or tone anywhere in the report (grep + page reading). The Molet 170-item wordlists (Mur and Kasu, Appendix E, image-only pages 51ff, inspected as rendered images) carry no stress marks.

sources.citation: McElhanon, Kenneth A. 1973. Towards a typology of the Finisterre-Huon languages, New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-22.
sources.harvard_location: DIV Offsite Storage - Ask at Circulation (Pamph. folio) BS 354.Z91
sources.note: Ch.1 Phonology treats ten representative languages (Kate, Ono, Selepet, Kube, Nabak, Uri, Wantoat, Kewieng, Rawa, Kovai), none from the Warup family; no stress statement at all, and Molet/Morafa appear only in the language list/map.

sources.citation: Claassen, Oren R. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11 (Pacific Linguistics A-23), 45-78.
sources.note: Sec. 2.2.3 subsumes Kasu and Somek (Molet-speaking villages per Carter et al. 2012) under 'Morafa' (=Asaro'o) with 'only slight dialectal differences'; the stock-wide phonology overview (6.1) remarks on stress only for Rawa, Yupna, Wantoat and Suroi — nothing for the Warup family/Morafa.
